Subject: Unexpected mid-month overage — need sample ledger and explanation

Hi team,

We noticed a ~38% jump in our usage line on the Nov 15 invoice vs. our historical baseline. The increase looks concentrated in conversational tokens (per your line item). We believe this is not driven by our traffic patterns — we didn't roll any feature changes or traffic spikes on the 14th–15th.

Can you provide:
- A sample ledger of requests (request id, timestamp, model, prompt tokens, completion tokens) for Nov 14–16 (a few hundred rows is fine).
- Any evidence of replays / duplicate ingestion events in that timeframe.
- Whether any model routing fallback or aux-model routing could have caused token multipliers.

We need this to justify a short-term hold on payment while we reconcile. Please reply with next steps and timeline.

Thanks,

Subject: Fwd: Unexpected mid-month overage — need sample ledger and explanation

Forwarding Alice's request — I took a first pass on telemetry. Summary of findings so far:

- We see a cluster of ~4.2k requests between 2026-11-14T23:40:00Z and 2026-11-15T02:05:00Z that have identical client_request_id values and almost-identical prompt payloads. That pattern strongly suggests a downstream replayer or retry loop from StellarPay's ingestion system (duplicate requests with same id). Our metering deduplication uses request_id + timestamp window; if the client_request_id is unique but identical across duplicates, and timestamps are within separate batches, they may bypass dedupe.
- No model routing fallbacks were triggered; all requests stayed on the primary conversational model (gpt-large-rc-v1). No aux-model multipliers detected.
- There's one minor fallback event earlier in the week (health check) but it is unrelated to the surge timeframe.

I'll include raw traces in a tarball and a CSV of flagged duplicate groups for Alice's team to cross-check. Proposed immediate actions:
1) Provide StellarPay the flagged-duplicates CSV (for matching on their side).
2) Offer provisional credit for the duplicated token usage while we jointly reconcile.
3) Add a short-term protection: enforce a stricter dedupe window for requests that present identical client_request_id values to avoid counting these duplicates across batches.

Notes: attached meter raw logs contain per-token attribution; it's large so I prepared a small tarball (metering-raw-logs-20261117.tar.gz).

Ben Carter
Billing & Metering Engineer
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: metering-raw-logs-20261117.tar.gz (raw traces, redacted PII)

Hi Vanessa / Ben — thanks for the quick look and the files. A couple quick notes from our side after matching against our ingestion logs:

- We do have a background replayer that attempted to backfill some events on 2026-11-15 due to a downstream queue lag. The team confirms a bug in the replayer where it didn't rotate client_request_id for retries; that matches the identical id pattern you flagged.
- We'll run a localized dedupe on our side and report back the set of true-duplicates. Can you confirm your provisional credit approach (percent or exact tokens) and how long before the overage hold is released?

Ideally we'd get a provisional credit and a corrected invoice so our AR/AP can continue processing payments. Please advise process and timeline.

Best,
Alice

Hi Alice — appreciated, and thanks to Ben for the quick triage. Proposed resolution steps: 

1) Provisional credit: we'll apply a provisional credit equal to the tokens flagged as duplicates in Ben's CSV (we'll mark this as provisional until your dedupe runs complete). The provisional credit will reflect token pricing at your current rate (per the RDW-5491 rate band).
2) Timeline: we'll post the provisional credit within 48 business hours and issue a corrected invoice within 5 business days after your confirmation of the dedupe results.
3) Permanent mitigation: Ben's team will enable the temporary stricter dedupe window for identical client_request_id within 7 days; we'll coordinate a change control RFC and confirm back to you.

Next steps for StellarPay: Please return the dedupe-verified list (or a confirmation that your localized run reduced the flagged set by X token count). Once we have that, we'll convert the provisional credit to a final invoice adjustment.

If you'd like a formal credit note or a DocuSign amendment for accounting, we can provide both. I've attached a draft credit note and included a link to the invoice page.

Thanks — looking forward to the confirmed list.

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Lead, Enterprise Customers
Redwood Inference
